messages:
liam: Quick heads-up — onboarding sample-apps failing nondeterministically because SDKs expose different error shapes for identical server responses. We need a plan.
anya: Can you give one concrete example we can test against?
liam: Sure. Server returns 429 with Retry-After and body: { "code": "RATE_LIMIT", "message": "Too many requests", "request_id": "r_xyz" }
- Node: SDK error has status=429, headers.retry_after=30, body parsed -> good.
- Python: SDK throws RateLimitError(message="Too many requests") with no request_id or retry_after attr.
- Kotlin: exception.text == "429 Too Many Requests" and no structured payload.
liam: Those discrepancies force app authors to parse freeform strings or rely on fragile language-specific helpers.
gabi: That's the crux. We need a minimal, tiny error envelope every SDK maps to. Not a huge RFC, just the fields required for routing/retry.
trace: Proposal (minimal): code (string), status (int|null), message (string), retryable ("yes"|"no"|"unknown"), retry_hint (nullable string), retry_after (int seconds|null), request_id (string|null), legacy_message (string|null). Add envelope_version: "v1".
anya: Love explicit retry_after in seconds for clients that prefer header parsing. Also recommend machine_message to carry raw server body if present.
gabi: Keep envelope tiny. For streaming errors, runtime should emit one JSON line in the stream as the error frame so client libs can decode.
liam: Implementation sketch: runtime canonicalizer converts internal errors -> envelope JSON; SDK transport layer maps envelope -> typed exception object with getters. For transports where we can't get server body (e.g., TLS drop), SDK should synthesize envelope with code="NETWORK_ERROR" and retryable="unknown".
trace: SDK ergonomics: typed exceptions should implement methods get_status(), code(), is_retryable(), retry_after(). Also provide top-level helpers: sdk.IsRetryable(err) and sdk.RecommendedBackoff(err).
anya: Tests: add a tiny cross-language interop test in sample-apps that runs server mock returning 401/429 and asserts the SDKs expose envelope fields and helpers behave consistently. CI should run that matrix.
gabi: Migration: include legacy_message for a cycle; add docs section "How to migrate from parsing raw messages" with examples in Node/Python/Java.
liam: Owners: @gabi spec + docs, @trace runtime canonicalizer POC, @anya sample-app interop tests, @liam coord SDK follow-ups. Target: spec + sample-app test in 5 business days; runtime + SDKs proto within next sprint.
ci-bot: queued job: sample-apps/interop-error-envelope (matrix node, python, kotlin)
trace: I'll open a small WIP PR for runtime canonicalizer and post link here when ready.
anya: I'll add a short quickstart blurb showing: try { ... } catch (err) { if (sdk.IsRetryable(err)) { sleep(sdk.RecommendedBackoff(err)); retry(); } } with examples.
gabi: One more nuance: prefer 'retryable' tri-state to avoid apps assuming false positives. Also call out permanent auth errors vs transient rate limits in the spec.
liam: Great. This should cut onboarding friction a lot and make our sample apps reliable. I'll follow up with a checklist for reviewers. :thumbsup:
